{{nihongo|'''Kamiichinomiya Ōawa Shrine'''|上一宮大粟神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

'''Kamiichinomiya Ōawa Shrine''' (かみいちのみやおおあわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} on {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mt. Ōawa}} in {{ill|Kamiyama, Tokushima|Q1350922|qid=Q1350922}}, {{ill|Myōzai District, Tokushima|ceb|Myōzai Gun|es|Distrito de Myōzai|fr|District de Myōzai|id|Distrik Myōzai, Tokushima|it|Distretto di Myōzai|ja|名西郡|ko|묘자이군|pl|Powiat Myōzai|uk|Повіт Мьодзай|zh|名西郡|qid=Q1155732}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|Q160734|qid=Q160734}}. It is one candidate shrine for "Ame-no-Iwato-wake Yakura-hime Shrine," a {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288|qid=Q134917288}} and ichinomiya of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|be|Ава (правінцыя, Сікоку)|cs|Provincie Awa (Tokušima)|de|Provinz Awa (Tokushima)|es|Provincia de Awa (Tokushima)|fa|ولایت آوا|fr|Province d'Awa (Tokushima)|gl|Provincia de Awa, Tokushima|id|Provinsi Awa (Tokushima)|it|Awa (provincia, Tokushima)|ja|阿波国|ko|아와국 (난카이도)|lt|Avos žemė (Tokušima)|nl|Awa (Tokushima)|pt|Província de Awa (Tokushima)|ru|Ава (Сикоку)|simple|Awa Province (Tokushima)|sk|Awa (provincia, Tokušima)|sr|Провинција Ава (Шикоку)|tr|Awa (vilayet, Tokushima)|uk|Провінція Ава (Шікоку)|zh|阿波國|zh_min_nan|Awa-kok (Nankaidô)|qid=Q907457}}<ref>Other candidate shrines are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yakura-hime Shrine}} and {{ill|Ichinomiya Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|一宮神社 (徳島市)|simple|Ichinomiya Shrine (Tokushima)|zh|一宮神社 (德島市)|qid=Q11352598|lt=Ichinomiya Shrine}}.</ref>. Its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is temple No.73 of the {{ill|Shin-Shikoku Mandara Pilgrimage|Q11501519|qid=Q11501519}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Ōgetsuhime|Q3261482|qid=Q3261482|lt=Ōgetsuhime-no-Mikoto}} (おおげつひめのみこと) - also called Ame-no-Iwato-wake Yakura-hime-no-Mikoto or Ōawa-hime-no-Mikoto.

According to shrine tradition, Ōgetsuhime came on horseback from Niu-no-gō in {{ill|Ise Province|Q864166|qid=Q864166}} (present {{ill|Nyū|ja|丹生 (多気町)|qid=Q17213591|lt=Niu}}, {{ill|Taki, Mie|arz|تاكى|ceb|Taki-chō|ckb|تاکی|es|Taki (Mie)|fa|تاکی، میئه|fr|Taki (Mie)|hy|Տակի|id|Taki, Mie|it|Taki (Giappone)|ja|多気町|ko|다키정|ms|Taki, Mie|my|တခိမြို့၊ မိအဲ|pl|Taki|ru|Таки (посёлок)|sr|Таки|sv|Taki, Mie|tl|Taki, Mie|tr|Taki, Japonya|uk|Такі (Міє)|ur|ٹاکی، میے|uz|Taki (Mie)|vi|Taki, Mie|zh|多氣町|qid=Q1203963}}, {{ill|Taki District, Mie|ceb|Taki-gun|ckb|گەڕەکی تاکی|es|Distrito de Taki|fr|District de Taki|id|Distrik Taki, Mie|it|Distretto di Taki|ja|多気郡|ko|다키군|pl|Powiat Taki (Mie)|uk|Повіт Такі|zh|多氣郡|qid=Q1042360}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}) to Awa Province and spread millet in this area.

In the Heian period, {{ill|Ichinomiya Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|一宮神社 (徳島市)|simple|Ichinomiya Shrine (Tokushima)|zh|一宮神社 (德島市)|qid=Q11352598|lt=Ichinomiya Shrine}} was founded in present {{ill|Ichinomiya-chō|ja|一宮町 (徳島市)|qid=Q11352592|lt=Ichinomiya-chō}}, {{ill|Tokushima (city)|Q207309|qid=Q207309}}, as a branch of this shrine.

In Meiji 3 ({{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}}), the shrine name was changed to "Haniu-meya Shrine," but by petition of parishioners it became the current Kamiichinomiya Ōawa Shrine in Meiji 28 ({{ill|1895|Q7844|qid=Q7844}}).
=== Precinct ===
* Great torii
* Shinmon gate: with sacred statues on both sides; from here the first half of the approach is earth path and the second half steep stone steps to the precinct
* Main shrine haiden and honden
* Sessha: Yasaka Shrine
* Sessha: small shrine to the right of shrine office
* Sessha: Akiba Shrine
* Ōawayama Jingū-ji: Shikoku 33 Kannon site No.4, Kōyasan Shingon, principal image Monju Bosatsu, founded in 729 by Gyōki as this shrine's bettō temple by imperial order of Emperor Shōmu
Past the large white torii is the shinmon gate, and stone steps from there lead up to the precinct. Taking the road right of the great torii, at the final fork left leads to this shrine and right to Jingū-ji. Up to microbus size can pass. There is broad parking around the main shrine.
